# FlashMP

> CPU matrix profiles for numeric time series. Use FlashMP to find recurring shapes (motifs), inspect unusual windows (discords), detect similar train/test subsequences, or give a tool-using agent a summary of a signal.

## Interfaces

- Python: `flashmp.stump(values, m)` takes an ordered numeric sequence and a window length in samples. `P_[i]` gives the z-normalized distance to the nearest eligible neighbor of window i. `I_[i]` gives that neighbor's start index. Constant windows are masked in the univariate self-join.
- Streaming: `flashmp.StreamMP(m=..., window=..., egress=True)` maintains a profile as old samples expire.
- Evaluation: `flashmp.scan_leakage(train, test, m=...)` flags correlated subsequences, including sign-flipped matches by default.
- CLI: `flashmp mp metrics.csv --col latency_ms -m 64 --out profile.csv` writes the profile to CSV.
- MCP: `flashmp-mcp` runs a local stdio server. `ts_digest` accepts numeric values or a file path. `ts_drilldown` takes the result's session handle plus `start` and exclusive `end` to retrieve the original samples.

## Run it

Install from GitHub with Git, Python 3.10+ and g++ or clang++ with C++20 support. The first native operation builds and caches the shared library.

- [Install command and expected output](https://github.com/pgg898200-ship-it/flashmp#find-the-second-occurrence)
- [Executable motif search notebook](https://github.com/pgg898200-ship-it/flashmp/blob/main/examples/find_a_repeated_shape.ipynb)
- [Python and command-line examples](https://github.com/pgg898200-ship-it/flashmp#python-and-command-line-examples)
- [Agent workflow and MCP tool list](https://github.com/pgg898200-ship-it/flashmp/blob/main/SKILL.md)
